verification.notes: Position-complete at the preferred level: all nine preferred elements are met in operative language, so the redline may be accepted as drafted even though the fallback checklist is not independently complete (no "worldwide" and no sublicence right on the embedded TrueLink IP grant). The Section 8(d) edit removes exactly the offending exploitation verbs (use, distribute, disseminate, license, resell, exploit) and substitutes a service-delivery purpose limitation; the heading, the nonexclusive/worldwide framing and the Non-Competition Agreement cross-reference are retained, so nothing outside the target element is disturbed. The inserted Client Ownership clause is a concise insertion filling a genuine gap (the Agreement contained no ownership/assignment, data-retention or anti-joint-ownership language) and adds no survival tail, expense, remedy or procedure. The added words "Client's Intellectual Property" and "including all results of the Support Services" are declaratory and within the rule's scope, so minimality is preserved, but they are the only clauses that could be trimmed if the counterparty pushes back. Intent is preserved: Section 2(d)'s Interface ownership is untouched and consistent with the new grant; no cross-reference is orphaned. Note that the 31-day/archiving mechanics in the Credit Data definition existed to delimit TrueLink's downstream data use — they remain operable as a definitional filter, but flag internally that their commercial purpose is diminished once the licence is narrowed. Drafting check before sending: confirm "Client Content", "Client's Intellectual Property", "TrueLink Intellectual Property" and "Hosting and Support Services" match defined terms used elsewhere in the Agreement; if any are undefined, replace with the defined equivalents (e.g. "Client Proprietary Information", "Support Services") to avoid an undefined-term defect. Optional hardening (not required for preferred completeness): add "worldwide" and a right to sublicense to the embedded TrueLink IP licence so the clause also clears the fallback checklist if TrueLink resists the assignment.

quote: IN NO EVENT SHALL TRUELINK'S LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11 THIS AGREEMENT (OTHER THAN DUE TO A BREACH RESULTING FROM TRUELINK'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT) EXCEED THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD.
rationale: The only liability limitation in the Agreement (p0077, inside the indemnity section) caps TrueLink alone at 12 months' hosting and support compensation, while Client's liability — including the very broad Section 12(a) indemnity — remains unlimited. That is walk-away territory under the rule (Customer uncapped while Vendor capped), and the sole carve-out covers only TrueLink's gross negligence and wilful misconduct, with nothing for indemnification or confidentiality (Section 10). We therefore target the fallback with the smallest edit: "TRUELINK'S LIABILITY" becomes "EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY" so the cap binds both parties, and the parenthetical carve-out is made mutual and extended to indemnification obligations and breach of confidentiality obligations. The existing Section 3, 4, 7 and 11 scope and the 12-month compensation basis are retained verbatim, so TrueLink gains no new cap protection for matters (e.g. warranties, service performance) where it is presently uncapped. Preferred items not pressed here: the USD 1,000,000 floor, "paid or payable", anchoring the window to the event giving rise to the claim, a mutual indirect/consequential exclusion, carve-outs for data protection/security, fraud and IP infringement, and the payment-obligations exclusion.

verification.notes: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative wording: mutual "EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY" cap, retained 12-month fee basis, and a mutual carve-out naming indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. Position-complete at the fallback; the finding is correctly a deviation with a fallback-targeted redline. Preferred level fails on six elements: no USD 1,000,000 floor and no "paid or payable"/event-giving-rise-to-the-claim anchor; no mutual indirect/consequential exclusion; and no carve-outs for data protection and security, fraud, or infringement of the other party's IP; and no statement that Client's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap. To reach preferred the drafter would need to insert those items in operative text, not merely note them. Minimality holds: only the liability subject and the carve-out parenthetical were touched; the Section 3, 4, 7 and 11 scope and the hosting-and-support 12-month compensation basis survive verbatim, and no survival tail, expense language or extra damages categories were added. Re-phrasing "DUE TO A BREACH RESULTING FROM TRUELINK'S" into "A PARTY'S" is necessary to mutualise and list the four carve-outs, so it is not a gratuitous deletion. Intent preserved: no defined term is left dangling, no cross-reference is broken, and TrueLink gains no new cap protection outside the pre-existing Section 3/4/7/11 scope. One residual reading to watch (rationale note, not a defect requiring repair at fallback): because the cap is now mutual, Client's obligation to pay compensation could be argued to be capped — a short "Client's payment obligations are not subject to this limitation" sentence would close that and also advance a preferred element. Two further rationale-level notes for negotiation, not fallback failures: (i) the cap measure is "compensation paid for hosting and support services" rather than all fees under the Agreement — confirm hosting/support compensation is not a small subset of total consideration, or the cap risks being illusory; (ii) "THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD" has no express anchor (claim or event), which is retained legacy language.

quote: 15. ASSIGNMENT OR TRANSFER. Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
rationale: Section 15 is the only assignment provision in the Agreement. It bars assignment by either party without the other's prior written approval, with a mutual carve-out only for a "financially responsible affiliate". It fails the fallback because there is no successor right at all (no merger/acquisition/asset-sale carve-out, no successor-with-notice construct) and no reasonableness standard on consent; the retained no-consent affiliate exception also cannot coexist with a fallback under which every non-successor assignment requires consent. Rather than strip our own affiliate right to reach fallback, we move to the preferred position: Client-only affiliate and successor assignment without approval, TrueLink assignment only with our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a competitor. No change-of-control termination right exists today, so the added confirmation is a clarification only.

quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: Section 14 (p0079) gives Client an unconditional, no-cause election to terminate the Agreement at any time — a convenience right even though the word "convenience" is not used — with service simply continuing until the last day of the month following the month of notice (roughly 30-60 days' run-off). That is at or better than the fallback notice window of 60-90 days, and no early-termination fee, penalty or other exit charge appears anywhere in the Agreement, so the three-months-of-fees fee cap is comfortably satisfied. On the Vendor side, TrueLink has no mid-term termination-for-convenience right: Section 13 (p0078) permits mid-term cutting-off of Sections 2 and 3 only for Client breach/default events (for cause), and the only other exit is the mutual auto-renewal non-renewal notice given "no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year," whose effect is expressly tied to the end of the then-current one-year term — that is natural-term non-renewal reviewed under RENEWAL, not a Vendor mid-term convenience right, so we do not flag it twice here. The initial term is one year, so the walk-away concern about no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term does not arise. Falling short of the preferred position only in that there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; this is immaterial because Section 5(a) (p0045) has TrueLink invoice monthly with invoices "paid within 15 days of receipt," so fees are not prepaid. The clause therefore sits at (and in the Customer's favour, above) the fallback and we would not redline it.

Nothing therefore needs frequency, notice, business-hours, independent-auditor, cost-allocation or system-access limits, and no walk-away risk (unlimited/unannounced audits or remote access to Client systems) is present. No repair is required if the fallback is the chosen target. Minimality holds. Only two insertions were made, each traceable to a selected fallback element; § 2(a)'s Customer-favourable non-exclusivity/alternative-sourcing sentence and § 2(c) are untouched, and the retained mutual affiliate assignment exception is preserved rather than deleted (the ASSIGN fallback bar on non-successor exceptions is not part of this checklist). No duplicate coverage arises because "Client" is defined as Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. alone, so the affiliate extension is not redundant; and because a grant to an affiliate carries use through its authorised personnel, no separate personnel/access edit was (correctly) attempted. The § 15 edit is drafted as a direct, narrowly scoped exception to the existing consent mechanic rather than a broad notwithstanding override, so the retained consent requirement is not contradicted and no dangling cross-reference or undefined term is created; unrelated allocation, timing, and commercial mechanics survive intact. Minor drafting nit (not a failure): in § 2(a) the field-of-use phrase "in the ordinary course of its business" now follows a two-party grant; the drafter may wish to render it "their respective businesses" for clarity, but as written it does not defeat any checklist element.

Fallback elements are conditional on a surviving commitment; because the commitment is deleted outright, the 12-month limit, 30-day reduction right, and true-up mechanic have no subject matter and are satisfied without needing operative text. quote: This Agreement shall renew automatically thereafter for successive one year periods until terminated pursuant to Section 12 herein or unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year.

Each renewal term is 12 months (no multi-year renewal, so no walk-away exposure) and Client's non-renewal notice window is 30 days, satisfying both the fallback ceiling of 60 days and the preferred 30-day opt-out. On price, renewal permits no unilateral uplift: fees are fixed by the schedules in Exhibits A and B (p0045), Section 6 freezes Hosting Services costs for the first year and adds an MFN that rates will not exceed those charged to any other party (p0047), and Section 16 requires any amendment to be in writing and signed by the party to be charged, so any increase at renewal needs Client's agreement and the conditional price-cap element is not triggered. The only shortfall against preferred is the absence of a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; that is a minor sub-element we note rather than redline. The clause meets the fallback (and most of preferred) on its material terms and needs no change.

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall (a) at Client's request, provide transition assistance for up to six (6) months following such expiry or termination, at TrueLink's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days following such expiry or termination, return all Client Content and other Client data in TrueLink's possession or control in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) after such return, delete such Client Content and Client data from its systems and certify such deletion to Client in writing.

verification.notes: Preferred level is complete: 14a covers the expiry-or-termination trigger, six months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day return in a commonly used machine-readable format, and post-return certified deletion. The rule is a 'missing clause' insertion, so wholly new wording can still be minimal; the drafter inserted a single concise paragraph and did not delete or alter any existing language in Sections 13 or 14 (both are rendered verbatim). No extras beyond the checklist: no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no added remedies, damages categories or procedures. 'in TrueLink's possession or control' and 'at Client's request' track the model language and are needed to make the return and assistance obligations operable. Data scope is drafted broadly ('all Client Content and other Client data'), so it is not limited to selected named data types; it captures the borrower/loan data referenced in the comment. Intent is preserved: Section 13's name-server (30 days) and hosting-environment (60 days) migration duties on Client and Client's retained ownership of domains and Client Content survive without contradiction, as does Section 14's month-end wind-down of Hosting and Support Services; 14a operates after that wind-down and creates no dangling cross-reference or undefined term ('Client Content' and the parties are defined). Comment is compliant in tone, explains the change and cites the fallback without lecturing.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 9 gives us only a Year 2000 warranty, so TrueLink stands behind nothing else in its performance. We have added our fallback warranty: 90-day software conformance to documentation, 30-day services warranty, with repair, replacement or refund as the remedy.

ops.text: TrueLink further represents and warrants that (i) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, the Interface and all related software will conform in all material respects to its documentation, and (ii) for a period of thirty (30) days following performance, the Hosting Services and Support Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner. Client's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at TrueLink's option, repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or Services, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming software or Services.

quote: 9. TRUELINK WARRANTIES. TrueLink represents and warrants that the Interface and all related software (i) is designed to be used before, on and after January l, 2000;
rationale: TrueLink's only warranty (Section 9) is a Year 2000 date-processing warranty; there is no warranty that the Interface or related software conforms to its documentation, no services warranty, and no repair/replace or refund remedy anywhere in the Agreement (searches for documentation/conformance and refund/re-performance remedies returned nothing; Sections 3 and 4 impose only reasonable-efforts hosting and support obligations). That fails every fallback element, so we insert the shortest fallback warranty: 90-day software conformance to documentation, 30-day services warranty, and repair, replacement or refund. The Section 12 disclaimer is prefaced \"EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT,\" so it does not swallow the inserted express warranty and needs no amendment.

verification.notes: Fallback checklist is complete: 90-day software-to-documentation warranty, 30-day services warranty, and repair/replacement or refund remedy all appear in operative language, not merely in the comment. Preferred level is not reached: the software period is 90 days rather than 12 months, the services period is 30 days rather than 90 days, and there is no compliance-with-laws or no-malicious-code warranty. Classification as a deviation cured to fallback is correct. Minimal: the edit is a single concise insertion into the existing Section 9; the Year 2000 warranty, the evidence/repair mechanics and the Section 12 disclaimer are all retained verbatim, with no deletions, survival tails, expense language or extra procedures added. The 'professional and workmanlike' standard is the necessary substantive content of the 30-day services warranty, not an extra. Preserves intent: the Section 12 disclaimer is already prefaced "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT," so it does not swallow the new express warranty and correctly required no amendment; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are created (Hosting Services and Support Services are defined). Optional drafting nit (not a failure): the remedy sentence says "this warranty" while the preceding sentence contains two warranties — consider "these warranties" to avoid any argument that the remedy attaches only to the conformance limb.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no insurance provision even though TrueLink hosts our Web Site and processes our and our customers' data, so we have added a short insurance clause at our standard levels (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request). If helpful, we can fall back to E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

ops.text: INSURANCE. TrueLink shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; where TrueLink processes any data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Client, cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000; and workers' compensation insurance as required by law. TrueLink shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

proposal.summary: Insert a new Section 31 requiring TrueLink to carry CGL, E&O, cyber/privacy and workers' compensation insurance and to provide certificates on request.

quote: 30. FORCE MAJEURE. TrueLink will be excused from delays in performing or from failing to perform its obligations under this Agreement to the extent the delays or failures result from causes beyond the reasonable control or TrueLink.
rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance obligation anywhere: searches for insurance, coverage, certificates and workers' compensation return nothing (the only "insur" hit is "mortgage insurers" in the recitals), and the general provisions (Sections 13-30, p0078-p0097) address term, termination, assignment, notices, law, venue and force majeure but never insurance. TrueLink hosts our Web Site and transmits Client and consumer credit data, so the absence of any cover is walk-away territory under the playbook. We insert a short new Section 31 at the preferred level (CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M where TrueLink processes data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Client, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request), with fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M available. No survival tail or expense language was added beyond the checklist elements.

verification.notes: All six preferred elements appear in the inserted operative sentence with the correct amounts, bases and party direction (TrueLink as insuring party, Client as beneficiary of the data trigger). The insertion omits the model language's extras — "at its own expense" and the one-year survival tail — consistent with the instruction that such model-language additions are non-minimal unless a selected element requires them. The cyber trigger is drafted as "any data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Client," satisfying the requirement that the Customer Data insurance trigger cover every category rather than named data types. Retained Section 30 (force majeure) is untouched; no words outside the target elements were deleted or paraphrased, and the new stand-alone insurance paragraph creates no undefined term or dangling cross-reference ("TrueLink" and "Client" are defined in the preamble). Concise insertion for a genuinely missing clause: deterministic checks confirm no pre-existing insurance obligation elsewhere, so wholly new wording is appropriate and no duplicate operative coverage is created.
